parts:
Hi, 

I am running a hierarchal model on binary (0/1) variables with missing data. My later goals are (1) to run MIMIC models with this hierarchal model and (2) to extract factor scores for (P, f1, f2, and f3). However, I get 4 warnings and do not know how to deal with warnings 2-4. The problem appears to stem from factor f1 but I do not know how to fix it. 

I attached the code and some data for a reproducible example. 

Thank you very much for your help. 

Camille

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Hierarchal CFA Binary Variables Missing Data
parts:
It is easier to simply set std.lv=TRUE than free first loadings and fix factor variances.  But in this case I think you should stick with the default method of fixing the first loading and freeing the factor variances.  It looks like the P=~f1 loading is trying its hardest to become orders of magnitude larger than its residual variance, which you have fixed to 1 (so it can't compensate by approaching zero).   In fact, before fitting a higher-order factor, just fit a CFA with the 3 lower-order factors.  With only 3 factors, that is statistically equivalent anyway, but you could take a look at the factor correlations and see whether a higher-order factor really fits the "observed" pattern.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hi Terrence, 

Thank you for your feedback. 

As in the hierarchal model, I get negative observed variable variance for Bipolar Disorder when I perform a CFA with the 3 lower-order factors with and without std.lv = T. This negative variance problem is resolved when loading the observed variables of f3 (Bipolar + Schizophrenia) directly onto the P-Factor. 

Question 1: How do I know from the factor correlations that a higher-order factor really fits the "observed" pattern? I included my code with the factor correlations and covariance. 

Question 2: Why would you suggest not using std.lv = T to estimate factor scores? When I look at the correlation between the factor scores (P, f1, and f2) that I extract from the models with std.lv = T and std.lv = F using the EBM method with missing data, I get a perfect correlation.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Hierarchal CFA Binary Variables Missing Data
parts: Question 1: How do I know from the factor correlations that a higher-order factor really fits the "observed" pattern?

I just wondered why the higher-order factor was having trouble capturing covariances among only 3 indicators.  It can be problematic when one of the indicators does not really correlate with the other 2.  But your next question provides additional information that is probably the explanation.
Question 2: Why would you suggest not using std.lv = T to estimate factor scores?

Standardization has nothing to do with estimating factor scores (which have an arbitrary metric anyway).  I suggested not fixing the first-order residual factor variances to 1 because that first factor loading was getting huge.  I thought perhaps the ML solution might be one in which the residual variance was nearly zero, even negative, which makes it problematic to fix that value to 1.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
